page: Microsoft Azure E20s_v7 is an Esv7-family virtual machine configured with 20 dedicated vCPUs and 160.0 GB of system memory. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server features 10 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and INT8 operations.

This server does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is premium storage capable, allowing connection to external Azure storage volumes. It runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The memory configuration provides a high density of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, aligning the instance with memory-optimized resource profiles.

Benchmark data shows average performance across most compute and memory operations, with specific strengths in compression and small-model inference. The single-core stress-ng score is 2232.95, and the multi-core score is 20536.75. Single-threaded gzip compression at 35.43 GB/sec and single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 14.68 GB/sec both rank in the top 25%. For machine learning workloads, the server achieves top-tier performance in text generation for a small 135M LLM model at 364.6 tokens per second, while prompt processing for the same model averages 2226.42 tokens per second. Large-block memory read bandwidth is measured at 139.09 GB/sec, and write bandwidth is 57.2 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E20s_v7 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it suitable for memory-intensive workloads without the overhead of paying for excess compute cores. The presence of Intel AMX instructions provides hardware acceleration for certain AI inference tasks without requiring a dedicated GPU. This virtual machine is designed for workloads such as database operations, memory-cached applications, enterprise applications, and lightweight LLM text generation.
